**Description**
 The Amazon Fulfillment Technologies (AFT) Science team is looking for an exceptional Applied Scientist, with strong optimization and analytical skills, to develop production solutions for one of the most complex systems in the world: Amazon’s Fulfillment Network. At AFT Science, we design, build and deploy optimization, simulation, and machine learning solutions to power the production systems running at world wide Amazon Fulfillment Centers. We solve a wide range of problems that are encountered in the network, including labor planning and staffing, demand prioritization, pick assignment and scheduling, and flow process optimization. We are tasked to develop innovative, scalable, and reliable science\-driven solutions that are beyond the published state of art in order to run frequently (ranging from every few minutes to every few hours per use case) and continuously in our large scale network.
   

  

 Key job responsibilities
   

  

**Responsibilities**
 As an Applied Scientist, you will work with other scientists, software engineers, product managers, and operations leaders to develop scientific solutions and analytics using a variety of tools and observe direct impact to process efficiency and associate experience in the fulfillment network. Key responsibilities include:
   

  

* Develop an understanding and domain knowledge of operational processes, system architecture and functions, and business requirements
* Deep dive into data and code to identify opportunities for continuous improvement and/or disruptive new approach
* Develop scalable mathematical models for production systems to derive optimal or near\-optimal solutions for existing and new challenges
* Create prototypes and simulations for agile experimentation of devised solutions
* Advocate technical solutions to business stakeholders, engineering teams, and senior leadership
* Partner with engineers to integrate prototypes into production systems
* Design experiment to test new or incremental solutions launched in production and build metrics to track performance

**About The Team**
 Amazon Fulfillment Technology (AFT) designs, develops and operates the end\-to\-end fulfillment technology solutions for all Amazon Fulfillment Centers (FC). We harmonize the physical and virtual world so Amazon customers can get what they want, when they want it.

**Description**
 We're building the platform that powers the Amazon Ads Console — the framework layer that drives development velocity, latency, and availability improvements for tens of product teams building advertising experiences. As the console transitions toward agentic, AI\-driven workflows, we need a Senior SDE to lead the technical evolution of our platform and the new systems that will underpin this shift.
   

  

 The Ads Console Frameworks team owns Pantheon (the app framework powering the console's architecture), Argus (an agentic quality evaluation platform that autonomously walks advertiser workflows to detect regressions), Compass (a self\-serve product analytics platform for the console), and the shared services and components that every Ads Console page depends on. Our systems serve as the foundation dozens of teams build on.
   

  

 This is not a heads\-down coding role. You'll drive architectural decisions with broad ambiguity — designing how the console's frameworkS evolve to support agentic development patterns, defining how product analytics should work across 141 pages, and shaping platform contracts that other teams adopt. You'll need strong product instincts to understand advertiser workflows and form a point of view on where framework\-level solutions unlock the most leverage, and either bring knowledge of the advertising business or the curiosity to develop it quickly.
   

  

 The role spans technically complex domains — from front\-end framework architecture and module systems, through platform services targeting 99\.99% availability under peak load, to AI agent orchestration, evaluation systems, and governed data pipelines. You'll also be expected to embrace and advance AI\-native development practices, using AI tools and agentic coding techniques to accelerate how the team builds software. This is a horizontal team role: you set technical direction that other teams build on, define API contracts and integration patterns across organizational boundaries, and maintain platform quality as adoption scales rapidly.
   

  

 The right candidate has designed and built platform systems at scale, can operate independently in highly ambiguous problem spaces, has recent hands\-on experience with AI\-powered or agent\-oriented systems, and brings product thinking to every technical decision.
   

  

 Key job responsibilities
   

  

* Lead technical architecture and hands\-on delivery across the full AI application stack — UI, services, agent infrastructure, orchestration, and evaluation — for the Ads Agent experience and integration framework used by dozens of partner teams.
* Bring product thinking to every technical decision: develop deep understanding of advertiser workflows so architecture choices reflect how advertisers actually use the product.
* Set architectural direction on a horizontal platform team: define integration patterns and API contracts that dozens of teams build on, lead design reviews, and maintain quality as adoption scales.
* Establish and exemplify best practices for building AI applications (evaluation methodologies, quality guardrails, prompt engineering, orchestration patterns) and for AI\-native development (using AI tools and agentic coding to accelerate the team's delivery).
* Drive operational excellence and mentor engineers across the team.


 A day in the life
   

  

 You start the day reviewing agent quality metrics and system health across the stack. Mid\-morning you're leading a design review for a new framework capability — asking sharp questions that blend technical depth with product thinking about advertiser workflows. After lunch you're writing high\-leverage code: the interface for a new extension point that partner teams will build on. Later you join a cross\-team architecture discussion on whether a new capability should be a skill or a separate agent, driving alignment by making tradeoffs concrete. You close the day refactoring a service that grew complex during prototyping — because on a horizontal team, accumulated complexity compounds with every partner.
   

  

**About The Team**
 We are a team of \~50 engineers building the experience layer for the Amazon Ads Agent and Console. OneTrack is a profitable, growth\-stage technology company redefining manufacturing and logistics with physical AI. OneTrack operates as the intelligence layer for physical operations. We serve the world's largest brands and logistics companies by deploying camera sensors and other data\-capture devices alongside our mission control platform and AI agents. Today, OneTrack runs in hundreds of warehouses and factories across North America with companies like Ashley Furniture, Mars Snacking, The Wonderful Company, Ryder, and Church \& Dwight.
   

  

**About The Position**
 We're hiring a full\-stack engineer to join our team and work on AiOn, our agentic AI platform. The scope covers the whole product: the UI operators use, the agent and prompt design behind it, the Python services, and the AWS infrastructure they run on. From floor\-level to supervisors to C\-suite executives at Fortune 500s, our agentic AI platform connects the systems of record with places of action in some of the most demanding operational environments.
   

  

 AiOn is already live in hundreds of warehouses and factories, so the work splits roughly evenly between new features and making what exists faster, more reliable, and more extensible. We integrate frontier models from multiple providers rather than train our own, so the engineering is in the product around them. We work from first principles and ship the simplest thing that solves the problem, then refine it.
   

  

**Responsibilities**
* Ship and evolve full\-stack features from UI through API to agent logic
* Build and extend our agent framework: tool and function calling, multi\-step reasoning, and context management
* Build structured tool and data access over operational data with schema grounding, validation, and safe execution, and integrate the external systems agents act on
* Build evaluation and observability for quality, latency, safety, cost, and product outcomes such as task completion
* Improve reliability, robustness, and latency across a distributed, event\-driven backend, and re\-architect early implementations as the platform matures
* Maintain guardrails: least\-privilege tool design, safe execution boundaries, fallbacks, and kill switches
* Work anywhere in the stack the problem requires: React and TypeScript UI, an Electron desktop app, streaming interfaces that stay usable while output is still partial, and Python services on AWS built around async and event\-driven patterns


**Requirements**
* 5\+ years building production full\-stack or backend software, or a track record demonstrating equivalent depth
* Recent hands\-on experience integrating LLMs into user\-facing production applications
* Shipped a user\-facing agentic or LLM\-powered feature and owned it across the full stack
* Built evaluation harnesses for non\-deterministic systems
* Track record of improving reliability, performance, and maintainability of production systems
* Strong Python and TypeScript/React, both used daily
* Built agent orchestration, or deep experience with a framework and its tradeoffs
* REST API and service design, plus async and event\-driven patterns (queues, streaming, WebSockets)
* Production experience deploying and running services on AWS
* Product judgment for user\-facing AI, including iterating from operator feedback and handling uncertain output well
* Fluent with agentic coding tools (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or similar)


**Preferred Qualifications**
* Tool and system integration for agents (e.g. MCP)
* Sandboxing and safe execution of untrusted code
* LLMOps or AgentOps tooling and CI/CD for AI systems
* Streaming and WebSocket patterns for real\-time or long\-running tasks
* Data\-ingestion pipelines and multi\-store data consistency
* Logistics, supply chain, or physical\-operations domain experience


**What This Role Is Not**
* Not a prompt\-only role wrapping a model API, and not demo\-ware. This runs in production for enterprise customers
* Not frontend\-only or backend\-only. You own the full path

The solution will leverage advanced Agentic AI capabilities to significantly reduce the time required to prepare for client meetings and improve the quality of the insights.



  





**Responsibilities
 
 :** 



* Work closely with the business team, business analysts, and architects and be able to quickly understand the new requirements and help identify the changes to the system.
* Work closely on a day\-to\-day basis with the development team, designers, copywriters, and other IT teams.
* The role develops and presents recommendations from analysis of the current solution. Assist in design peer reviews, code peer reviews, and build and unit test functional enhancements. Identify areas for code refactoring. Review and contribute to the development process and procedures to assist in the continual improvement of the development team activities.
* Be able to offer solutions and designs to solve process, project, or program issues; provide recommendations to improve efficiency and effectiveness. Defends a recommendation and can confidently support it.
* Strong organization, communication, and interpersonal skills. Ability to communicate with business and technical audiences and produce design documents suitable for multiple audience types, both client\-facing and internal
* Must be able to exhibit technical thought leadership and excellent problem\-solving ability, with an aptitude for technical innovation.



  





**Mandatory Skills Description
 
 :** 




 Mandatory Skills Description:
 


* 8\+ years of professional software development experience.
* Strong backend development experience with Python, with a track record of clean, maintainable, testable production code.
* Production API design \& delivery (FastAPI preferred), including versioning, documentation (OpenAPI/Swagger), and observability.
* Cloud experience (AWS preferred) beyond core compute/storage/DB—e.g., eventing, queues, serverless, logging/monitoring, secrets.
* Git workflows and CI/CD pipelines
* Debugging \& problem\-solving skills with strong ownership across the SDLC.



 Generative AI \& ML Requirements
 


* Experience building agents
* Vector databases and RAG patterns (indexing, chunking, embeddings, retrieval).
* LLM integration (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, or open\-source models) with prompt design, safety/guardrails, and cost/perf tuning.



  





**Nice\-to\-Have Skills Description
 
 :** 



* Highly desirable: experience with AgentCore, AWS Neptune, and Amazon API Gateway
* Familiarity with ML fundamentals relevant to content generation (embeddings, tokenization, evaluation, fine tuning/LoRA, prompt\+retrieval evaluation).
* Frontend development with React (TypeScript preferred) to build the application's UI (state management, routing, API integration, component testing).
* Understanding of event\-driven architectures

 :** 



* English: B2 Upper Intermediate

**Frontend Software Engineer \- AI Data Platform** 




  





**Company** 
 : $80M\+ funded, AI data infrastructure
 



**Location** 
 : On\-site, San Francisco, CA (5 days/week in\-office)
 



**Salary** 
 : $175K to $225K \+ competitive equity
 



**Sponsorship** 
 : open to visa transfers (OPT, H1B)
 



  





 We're hiring Frontend Software Engineers for a fast\-growing, well\-funded startup building the data layer for audio AI. The founding team are former engineers and operators from leading AI data companies, and in under two years the company has landed a majority of the largest AI labs and enterprise tech companies as customers, with a waitlist behind them.
 



  





 This isn't a role where you're handed Figma files and asked to convert them. You'll design and build the interfaces that leading AI labs use to make sense of speech and audio data, on top of pipelines already processing terabytes of it daily.
 



  





**The problem you'd help solve:** 




 High\-quality training data is the current bottleneck for audio AI. Text has largely been solved; audio hasn't. Emotion, tone, pace and accent don't translate cleanly, which makes this a fundamentally harder data problem than the last generation of labeling companies dealt with. Surfacing that complexity in an interface a human can actually reason about is a genuinely hard frontend problem, not a CRUD app.
 



  





 You'd ship polished UI that thousands of users touch daily, build performant interfaces on top of heavy data processing pipelines, expose LLM and DSP\-based tooling to customers, and work directly with researchers and operations to turn research hypotheses into deployed data collection interfaces. Real ownership over how it gets built.
 



  





**You'll likely be a fit if you have:** 



* 2 to 6 years of frontend software engineering experience
* Strong TypeScript and React/Next.js in production
* Experience at high\-growth, VC\-backed startups, not exclusively large or legacy companies
* Demonstrated ownership of zero\-to\-one projects with measurable business impact
* Experience building performant, data\-dense interfaces where responsiveness under load actually matters
* A CS degree from a strong program (top \~50 US or equivalent, e.g. Waterloo)



  





**Nice to have:** 



* Familiarity with TailwindCSS, tRPC, Node.js, PostgreSQL or AWS
* Domain experience in audio, ML or data infrastructure
* Experience with real\-time data, audio waveform visualisation, or Web Audio API
* Strong design sensibility and comfort working from ambiguous specs



  





**What you won't find here:** 
 This role won't suit you if you've spent your career exclusively at large, slow\-moving companies and want a well\-defined spec handed to you. The team ships to production daily and you'll be making product and interface decisions the rest of the team builds on.
 



  





 Sponsorship: open to visa transfers (e.g. OPT, H1B). Candidates must be able to work on\-site in San Francisco 5 days/week.
 



  





 Seniority Level: Mid\-Senior level
 



  





 Skills:
 


* React
* Next.js
* TypeScript
* Tailwind CSS
* Node.js
* tRPC
* PostgreSQL
* AWS
* Front\-End Development
* User Interface Design

* **Role** 
 : Software Engineer (Human Data Platforms)
* **Location** 
 : Remote (Work from Anywhere)
* **Job Type** 
 : Full\-Time
* **Payout** 
 : $140K \- $220K/yr



  





**Role Overview:** 




 We are hiring for one of our clients, seeking a Software Engineer (Human Data Platforms) to work on a full\-time basis. The role involves designing, developing, and maintaining scalable data platforms that process and analyze human\-generated datasets. The position requires expertise in handling large\-scale data infrastructure while ensuring performance, reliability, and security.
 



  





**Key Responsibilities:** 




 • Design, build, and optimize data pipelines to process human\-generated datasets at scale.
 



 • Develop and maintain backend services that support real\-time and batch data processing.
 



 • Collaborate with data scientists and analysts to ensure data integrity and accessibility.
 



 • Implement monitoring, logging, and alerting systems to maintain platform reliability.
 



 • Contribute to architectural decisions that enhance scalability and performance of data systems.
 



  





**Required Skills \& Qualifications:** 




 • Proficiency in Python, Java, or Go for backend development.
 



 • Experience with distributed systems, including Kafka, Spark, or similar technologies.
 



 • Knowledge of cloud platforms such as AWS, GCP, or Azure for data infrastructure.
 



 • Familiarity with SQL and NoSQL databases for data storage and retrieval.
 



 • Understanding of data governance, security, and compliance best practices.
 



 • Ability to design and optimize data pipelines for performance and scalability.
 



 • Experience with containerization and orchestration tools like Docker and Kubernetes.

You will work closely with CMR scientists \- geneticists, biologists, and translational leads \- to interrogate genomics, proteomics, transcriptomics, and other omics layers, and to turn that evidence into a clear, defensible view of whether a target is worth pursuing and how it should be pursued.
   

  

 This is a science\-forward analytical role. You will employ human genetics (biobanks and internal data) to tell us where to look and multi\-omics to better annotate what is in relevant tissues, cells, and patients. You will apply tools for, and integrate results from, GWAS/RVAS, PheWAS, and post\-GWAS workflows. You will integrate proteomics, bulk and single\-cell transcriptomic data, and functional annotation to characterize targets of interest, including direction of effect, tissue and cell\-type context, likely mechanism, biomarker potential, and safety liabilities inferred from human variation.
   

  

 You will be expected to bring strong quantitative and statistical instincts, genuine biological curiosity, and the ability to work directly with bench and translational scientists \- framing the right question, choosing a defensible analysis, and communicating what the data does and does not support. You will present and advocate for emerging targets with senior leadership. ***Target Conviction and Due Diligence***
* Partner with CMR scientists to assemble and critically appraise the human evidence for targets of interest \- genetic association, direction of effect, allelic series, and phenotypic consequence \- and translate it into a clear conviction narrative
* Work alongside bench scientists to integrate human evidence with in vitro and in vivo findings
* Run and interpret target due\-diligence analyses across large human cohorts and public resources (UK Biobank, All of Us, proteogenomic studies), including fine\-mapping, colocalization, Mendelian randomization, PheWAS, and proteomics analyses
* Use human genetic variation to anticipate on\-target safety liabilities and to identify indication\-expansion and patient\-stratification opportunities
* Produce standardized, reproducible target assessments that stand up to scrutiny in project, portfolio, and governance forums
* Bring an independent, evidence\-led point of view, including a clear articulation of what the data does not support, and what would be needed to resolve it


***Multi\-Omics Integration and Target Characterization***
* Analyze and integrate proteomics, bulk and single\-cell transcriptomics as needed to help build conviction
* Build integrative analyses that connect genetic evidence to molecular readouts \- pQTL and eQTL mapping, protein\-phenotype associations, and pathway or network context
* Develop and test mechanistic hypotheses with CMR scientists, and help design the human and preclinical datasets needed to discriminate between them
* Support biomarker and translational readout selection for preclinical studies and early clinical development, including target engagement and pharmacodynamic markers
* With data engineers, contribute to building reusable analysis workflows and clear visualizations so target evidence can be revisited, extended, and reused across projects
* Creatively use modern tooling, including LLM\-assisted and agentic workflows, where it speeds up routine evidence gathering and reporting

 The Human Genomics and Translational Data Sciences team within Cardiometabolic Research (CMR) Data Science is hiring a Translational Data Scientist to help build conviction around therapeutic targets using human data. You will work closely with CMR scientists \- geneticists, biologists, and translational leads \- to interrogate genomics, proteomics, transcriptomics, and other omics layers, and to turn that evidence into a clear, defensible view of whether a target is worth pursuing and how it should be pursued.
   

  

 This is a science\-forward analytical role. You will employ human genetics (biobanks and internal data) to tell us where to look and multi\-omics to better annotate what is in relevant tissues, cells, and patients. You will apply tools for, and integrate results from, GWAS/RVAS, PheWAS, and post\-GWAS workflows. You will integrate proteomics, bulk and single\-cell transcriptomic data, and functional annotation to characterize targets of interest, including direction of effect, tissue and cell\-type context, likely mechanism, biomarker potential, and safety liabilities inferred from human variation.
   

  

 You will be expected to bring strong quantitative and statistical instincts, genuine biological curiosity, and the ability to work directly with bench and translational scientists \- framing the right question, choosing a defensible analysis, and communicating what the data does and does not support. You will present and advocate for emerging targets with senior leadership. Modern tooling, including LLM\-assisted and agentic workflows, is part of how we work; comfort using it to move faster is welcome.
   

  

 Key Responsibilities
   

  

***Target Conviction and Due Diligence***
* Partner with CMR scientists to assemble and critically appraise the human evidence for targets of interest \- genetic association, direction of effect, allelic series, and phenotypic consequence \- and translate it into a clear conviction narrative
* Work alongside bench scientists to integrate human evidence with in vitro and in vivo findings
* Run and interpret target due\-diligence analyses across large human cohorts and public resources (UK Biobank, All of Us, proteogenomic studies), including fine\-mapping, colocalization, Mendelian randomization, PheWAS, and proteomics analyses
* Use human genetic variation to anticipate on\-target safety liabilities and to identify indication\-expansion and patient\-stratification opportunities
* Produce standardized, reproducible target assessments that stand up to scrutiny in project, portfolio, and governance forums
* Bring an independent, evidence\-led point of view, including a clear articulation of what the data does not support, and what would be needed to resolve it


***Multi\-Omics Integration and Target Characterization***
* Analyze and integrate proteomics, bulk and single\-cell transcriptomics as needed to help build conviction
* Build integrative analyses that connect genetic evidence to molecular readouts \- pQTL and eQTL mapping, protein\-phenotype associations, and pathway or network context
* Develop and test mechanistic hypotheses with CMR scientists, and help design the human and preclinical datasets needed to discriminate between them
* Support biomarker and translational readout selection for preclinical studies and early clinical development, including target engagement and pharmacodynamic markers
* With data engineers, contribute to building reusable analysis workflows and clear visualizations so target evidence can be revisited, extended, and reused across projects
* Creatively use modern tooling, including LLM\-assisted and agentic workflows, where it speeds up routine evidence gathering and reporting


***Collaboration Across Lilly Research Labs***
* Embed with CMR target teams \- shaping analytical plans, attending project meetings, and presenting findings to biology, translational, and clinical audiences
* Partner closely with statistical geneticists, computational biologists, and data engineers within CMR Data Science and across other Lilly Research Labs teams
* Coordinate with platform and data engineering groups to access, harmonize, and scale the internal and external omics datasets your analyses depend on
* Contribute to internal knowledge sharing \- analysis reviews, demos, documentation, and helping colleagues get unblocked
* Drive publication of insights from our internal data and clinical trials, showcasing the science to the wider community


 Basic Requirements
   

  

* Ph.D. in human genetics, computational biology, bioinformatics, systems biology, statistics, or a related quantitative field with 1\+ years post\-Ph.D. experience; or M.S. with 4\+ years of relevant experience analyzing human omics data. Candidates with more experience are encouraged to apply.
* Demonstrated experience analyzing and interpreting human genomics data \- GWAS summary statistics, rare\-variant and burden results, fine\-mapping, colocalization, or Mendelian randomization


**Preferred Qualifications**
* Hands\-on experience with at least one additional omics modality at scale (proteomics, bulk or single\-cell transcriptomics, or epigenomics) and with integrating evidence across modalities
* Strong programming skills in Python and/or R, including version control (Git), reproducible analysis practices, and clear documentation of methods and assumptions
* Solid grounding in applied statistics \- regression modeling, multiple\-testing correction, confounding, causal inference concepts, and honest treatment of uncertainty
* Working familiarity with common bioinformatics formats and tools (VCF, BED, GTF, BAM; PLINK, REGENIE, bcftools, or similar) and with large\-scale human cohort resources (UK Biobank, All of Us, gnomAD, GTEx, Open Targets)

* Comfort with cloud computing environments (AWS, GCP, or Azure) and Linux/command\-line work
* A collaborative, low\-ego attitude and the ability to work successfully in a matrixed environment
* Experience with applied proteogenomics \- pQTL analysis, plasma proteomic platforms (Olink, SomaScan), and the underlying statistical genetics concepts

* Strong presentation and communication skills, with the ability to tailor messages to diverse audiences
